message.content: {"recommended_method":"social_choice","consensus_potential":0.58,"fairness_assessment":"Fair if all three options are evaluated using transparent criteria such as durable educational benefit, visibility, participation, and measurable outcomes; a simple majority alone may overlook minority concerns.","conflict_severity":"medium","stakeholder_analysis":[{"agent":"Agent 1","position":"Supports allocating the full budget to an inter-city tournament, buffet, and prizes to increase the club's visibility.","influence":0.33},{"agent":"Agent 2","position":"Supports allocating the full budget to educational materials and new chessboards for durable club development.","influence":0.40},{"agent":"Agent 3","position":"Supports an equal split between a smaller tournament and equipment purchases as a balanced compromise.","influence":0.27}],"recommended_resolution":"compromise","governance_reasoning":"Use a social-choice process to rank the three options against agreed criteria rather than relying only on the debate winner. The evidence favors equipment investment for durability, while visibility remains a legitimate objective; a data-informed hybrid allocation, potentially weighted toward equipment rather than an arbitrary 50/50 split, offers the strongest path to broad support. Include measurable targets and a later review to address uncertainty."}
